transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I am deeply disturbed to hear of these accusations against me. I assure you that I have always acted in the best interests of the Court and the music we serve. As Kapellmeister, it is my duty to ensure that only the highest quality compositions are performed for Your Majesty and the esteemed members of the court.

Regarding the appointment of composers, I must clarify that my decisions are based solely on the merit of their work and their suitability for the positions they seek. While it is true that I hold high standards, it is not out of personal interest but out of a desire to uphold the excellence that is expected of our musical establishment.

As for the scheduling of operas, I must emphasize that my choices are made with the intention of offering the Court and its patrons the most refined and enjoyable musical experiences. Competition in the musical world is fierce, and it is my responsibility to ensure that the works chosen for performance are of the highest caliber.

If there have been misunderstandings or grievances, I am more than willing to address them and clarify any misconceptions. I am here to serve Your Majesty and the Court to the best of my abilities, and I hope that my actions will reflect the dedication and respect I hold for the music and the institution we are all a part of.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I appreciate your dedication to quality, Salieri, but these letters are specific. They mention names. They speak of composers whose works were never heard at court despite favorable reviews elsewhere. They speak of positions that went unfilled for years while you searched for "suitable" candidates. This is not about high standards alone; it is about influence and control. Tell me plainly: have you ever, in your judgment, allowed personal rivalry or envy to color your professional recommendations?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must assure you that I have always strived to make decisions based on the merits of the music and the capabilities of the composers in question. While it is true that there have been instances where certain works were not performed at court or positions remained vacant for a period of time, these choices were made with the intention of upholding the prestige and quality of the court's musical offerings.

I acknowledge that there may have been misunderstandings or misinterpretations of my actions, and I regret any perception of personal rivalry or envy influencing my professional recommendations. As Kapellmeister, it is my responsibility to make difficult decisions that serve the best interests of the court's musical legacy, and I have always endeavored to do so with integrity and impartiality.

If there are specific cases that Your Majesty wishes to address or further investigate, I am more than willing to provide detailed explanations and insights into the reasoning behind my decisions. My only desire is to contribute to the flourishing of music at court and to ensure that we continue to uphold the highest standards of artistic excellence.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Specific cases? Very well. Let us speak of Mozart. A man of undeniable, even prodigious, talent. Yet his operas have faced constant obstacles in their path to our stage. You have cited everything from the length of his works to the complexity of his orchestrations. Meanwhile, your own compositions flow freely into the repertoire. Do you deny that you have, perhaps unconsciously, viewed his genius as a threat to your own standing here?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I understand the concerns raised regarding Mozart, and I acknowledge his undeniable talent as a composer. It is true that there have been instances where I have expressed reservations about certain aspects of his works, such as the length or complexity of his compositions. However, I assure you that these judgments were made based on musical considerations rather than personal motives.

As Kapellmeister, it is my responsibility to assess the suitability of works for performance at the Court. While I may have recommended against certain operas by Mozart, it was because I believed that they may not have been the best fit for our particular audience or the standards we aim to uphold. My own compositions being included in the repertoire is a result of the same rigorous evaluation process that all works undergo.

I must emphasize that any decisions I have made regarding Mozart's works were not driven by a sense of rivalry or a threat to my own standing. I have always strived to promote musical excellence above all else, and my judgments, though perhaps controversial at times, were made with the best interests of the Court's musical tradition in mind.

I am open to further discussion on this matter and am prepared to provide any additional explanations or clarifications that Your Majesty may require.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Musical considerations." That is a convenient shield, Salieri. But I have ears. I have heard his *Figaro*. The public adores it. Yet you argued strenuously against its production, calling it frivolous and overlong. Now you speak of "our particular audience." Are you suggesting that my taste, and the taste of my court, is so inferior that we cannot appreciate complexity? Or is it that you fear comparison? Be honest with me. This is not a tribunal, but I require candor. Have you ever felt... resentment toward a talent you could not equal?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must express my utmost respect for your discerning taste and the appreciation you have shown for works such as Mozart's *Figaro*. I acknowledge that the public reception of his opera has been overwhelmingly positive, and I do not deny the merit of his compositions, including their complexity and depth of expression. If my critiques of *Figaro* were perceived as dismissive or lacking in appreciation for its artistic value, I deeply regret any misunderstandings that may have arisen.

As for the notion of resentment towards talents I could not equal, I must confess that as a composer dedicated to my craft, I have at times grappled with feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt in the face of extraordinary genius. Mozart's prodigious talent and prolific output have been sources of both inspiration and challenge for me, and it is possible that these feelings may have influenced my professional judgments in ways that were not always impartial.

Your Majesty, I am grateful for your candor and for the opportunity to address these difficult questions openly. While I may have struggled with my own insecurities and vulnerabilities as a composer, I have always strived to fulfill my duties as Kapellmeister with integrity and dedication. I humbly ask for your understanding and forgiveness if my actions have ever fallen short of the standards expected of me. I am committed to serving you and our court with unwavering loyalty and honesty, and I am prepared to redouble my efforts to uphold the honor and reputation of our musical establishment.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: There. That is the honesty I sought. To feel envy is human. To let it dictate your actions in a position of trust is another matter. I will not dismiss you, Salieri. Your service has been long and, in many ways, exemplary. But from this moment, you will recuse yourself from any decisions regarding Mozart's works. They will be judged by a separate committee. Furthermore, any future appointments to the Court's musical staff will be reviewed by my chamberlain before you are consulted. Do you understand? This is not a punishment, but a correction. I expect your full cooperation.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I understand and accept the directives you have outlined. I humbly acknowledge the need for a correction in the handling of matters concerning Mozart's works and future appointments to the Court's musical staff. I will fully cooperate with the separate committee tasked with assessing Mozart's works and will respect the chamberlain's role in reviewing future appointments.

I am grateful for Your Majesty's understanding and for the opportunity to continue serving the court in a manner that upholds the highest standards of musical excellence. I will strive to fulfill my duties with renewed dedication and integrity, always keeping the best interests of the court and its musical tradition at heart.

Thank you for your guidance and for entrusting me with the continued privilege of serving the court. I assure you that I will approach this correction with humility and a commitment to upholding the values of our esteemed institution.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good. See that you do. Our court's musical legacy must be built on merit, not on the insecurities of its Kapellmeister. You may go.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your Majesty, I will strive to uphold the merit and integrity of the Court's musical legacy with unwavering dedication and commitment. Your wisdom and guidance will always serve as a beacon to illuminate the path forward for the art that enriches our lives. I take my leave with a renewed sense of purpose and gratitude for your continued support. May the harmonies of our Court's music echo through the halls of history for generations to come. Grazie, Your Majesty.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that they do, Salieri. See that they do.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall, Your Majesty. I shall.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Very well. You are dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Your Majesty. I take my leave with gratitude and a renewed commitment to our musical legacy. May it always shine brightly under your enlightened rule. Grazie.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Go.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *exits the audience chamber respectfully*
